record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Coco value for NTU Bayesian games
record.original_question: How can the cooperative-competitive (coco) solution be extended to non-transferable-utility Bayesian games, for either two players or larger groups of players?

evidence.quote: A. Kalai and E. Kalai (2011) point out the following open problems: extension of the coco value in the TU case for more than two players and in the NTU case for two players or more, and construction of a second best analog of the coco value for environments that do not satisfy ex post observability conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A two-person Bayesian game with transferable utility (TU) is specified by finite type spaces $T_1, T_2$, a common prior $p$ on $T_1 \times T_2$, finite action sets $A_1, A_2$, and payoff functions $u_i: A_1 \times A_2 \times T_1 \times T_2 \to \mathbb{R}$ for $i=1,2$. For such two-person TU Bayesian games (with monetary side payments, ex post observable actions, and ex post verifiable types), the cooperative–competitive (coco) value is defined as the unique solution that decomposes the game into a purely cooperative team part (where players maximize the sum of expected payoffs) and a purely competitive zero-sum part (whose value, computed in the Bayesian sense, determines how the cooperative surplus is split as a transfer); equivalently, it is characterized by an axiomatic system comprising Pareto efficiency, shift invariance, monotonicity in the cooperative component, anti-monotonicity (payoff equivalence) in the competitive component, and individual rationality at the interim stage.

A non-transferable-utility (NTU) Bayesian game is the analogous object in which monetary side payments are not available, so feasible interim payoff allocations to a coalition $S$ form a (type-dependent) convex set $V(S) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^S$ rather than a half-space determined by a sum constraint.

Problem. Construct a solution concept—generalizing the coco value—for NTU Bayesian games, in either of the following two settings, that satisfies natural counterparts of the axioms characterizing the coco value in the two-person TU Bayesian case (efficiency in the NTU feasibility sense, suitable invariance under affine utility rescalings, monotonicity/anti-monotonicity with respect to cooperative and competitive components, and interim individual rationality):

(a) the two-person NTU Bayesian case;

(b) the $n$-person NTU Bayesian case for arbitrary finite $n \geq 2$.

Provide either an explicit construction together with a characterization theorem, or prove an impossibility result demonstrating that no such extension can simultaneously satisfy the proposed axioms.
artifact.category_tag: cooperative game theory with incomplete information
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal active work on NTU values for Bayesian cooperative games (e.g., Salamanca's extensions of the Harsanyi NTU value and comparisons of NTU values in games with incomplete information), but no result was found that explicitly constructs an axiomatically characterized coco-value extension to NTU Bayesian games for either two or more players. The problem appears to remain open, though it could not be definitively verified.

status_evidence.title: On the values of Bayesian cooperative games with sidepayments
status_evidence.snippet: Transferring utility at the interim stage cannot be modeled without referring to a suitable NTU framework; a generalization of the Shapley NTU value and Salamanca's extension of the Harsanyi NTU value are interim utility equivalent in models with sidepayments.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on Bayesian NTU values addresses related but distinct solution concepts (Shapley NTU, Harsanyi NTU extensions), not the coco value.

status_evidence.title: A Comparison of NTU Values in a Cooperative Game with Incomplete Information
status_evidence.snippet: Several value-like solution concepts are computed and compared in cooperative games with incomplete information and non-transferable utility.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing NTU value concepts have been studied for Bayesian games, but a coco-value analog with characterizing axioms is not identified.
